policy.purpose: Single source of truth for the tools page (tools.html). The verifier (verify-tools-data.js) reads tools.html and ensures (1) every tool referenced on the page exists here, (2) every external URL on the page matches the URL we have on file for that tool, (3) every cost claim on the page matches the cost field here, (4) no fabricated review counts, ratings, or 'N+ users' stats ship in the markup, and (5) every featured stack on the page only references tool IDs that exist here.
policy.verified_facts: We only list tools whose free / free-tier / hardship-program claim is sourced from the tool's own public site. If a tool's hardship program ever quietly disappears, the entry has to be updated or removed.
policy.do_not_invent: No fabricated star ratings, review counts, '10,000+ users' stats, success rates, or invented testimonials. The cost categories below are the only structured claims we make.

cost_categories.free: 100% free forever, no credit card, no trial-then-bill.
cost_categories.free-tier: Free forever with limits; paid tier exists but is optional. No credit card required for the free tier.
cost_categories.free-for-unemployed: Has an explicit, publicly-documented program that waives or refunds fees for users who are unemployed or in financial hardship.
cost_categories.paid-with-discounts: Paid product, but they have a public discount, scholarship, or hardship pathway you can apply for.

tools.name: freeCodeCamp
tools.what: Free coding curriculum with certifications and real-world projects.
tools.why_for_layoff: 100% free, non-profit, no upsell. Self-paced — pick it up on the days you have energy.

tools.name: Khan Academy
tools.what: Free K-12, college, and adult learning across math, computing, finance, and more.
tools.why_for_layoff: Non-profit. Whole catalogue is free. Good for brushing up before technical interviews.

tools.name: ADPList
tools.what: Book free 1:1 calls with mentors in product, design, engineering, and marketing.
tools.why_for_layoff: 100% free for mentees. The mentors volunteer their time. Often the fastest way to get a real human's eyes on your situation.

tools.name: You Need A Budget (YNAB)
tools.what: Personal-finance app built around envelope-style budgeting and runway planning.
tools.why_for_layoff: Has a long-running, publicly-documented program: contact support if you're a student or unemployed and they extend your subscription for free for up to 12 months.
tools.hardship_program: Email support@ynab.com from your account address; tell them you're unemployed. They extend access for free.

tools.name: Pramp
tools.what: Free peer-to-peer mock technical interviews with anonymous matching.
tools.why_for_layoff: Free forever. Schedule a 1-hour mock with someone in your tier and swap roles half-way. No paid upgrade pressure.

tools.name: Interviewing.io
tools.what: Anonymous mock interviews with senior engineers from FAANG-tier companies.
tools.why_for_layoff: Free tier for software engineers. Records the call so you can review it without re-living it in real time.

tools.name: Yoodli
tools.what: AI speech coach that scores filler words, pacing, and clarity on practice videos.
tools.why_for_layoff: Free tier with unlimited recordings. Practice answering 'tell me about yourself' in private until your shoulders unclench.

tools.name: Teal
tools.what: Job tracker with a resume builder, AI-tailoring, and a Chrome clipper.
tools.why_for_layoff: Generous free tier covers tracking + resume + cover letter. Paid is optional. The 'job match score' is genuinely useful for triage.

tools.name: Huntr
tools.what: Kanban-style job application tracker with autofill and contact management.
tools.why_for_layoff: Free tier handles the basics. Useful when applying-from-bed and you can't remember which company sent which rejection.

tools.name: Simplify
tools.what: Browser extension that autofills job applications and tracks them in one inbox.
tools.why_for_layoff: 100% free. Cuts the soul-crushing 20-minute application form down to about two minutes per role.

tools.name: Resume Worded
tools.what: AI scoring for your resume and LinkedIn profile against real recruiter heuristics.
tools.why_for_layoff: Free tier gets you a couple of detailed scans per month. Useful sanity check before the apply spree.

tools.name: levels.fyi
tools.what: Real comp data submitted by tech employees, broken down by level and location.
tools.why_for_layoff: Free. Use it before any offer call so you don't lowball yourself out of fear.

tools.name: Comprehensive
tools.what: Compensation data scraped from public US job postings (post-pay-transparency-laws).
tools.why_for_layoff: Free. Wider coverage than levels.fyi for non-FAANG roles and non-engineering functions.

tools.name: Claude.ai
tools.what: Anthropic's general-purpose AI assistant (writing, code, research).
tools.why_for_layoff: Free tier, no credit card. Good for cover letters, story-mining your old work, and rehearsing answers to hard questions.

tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.what: OpenAI's general-purpose AI assistant.
tools.why_for_layoff: Free tier with no credit card. Same use cases as Claude — cover letters, mock Qs, untangling job descriptions.

tools.name: Google Gemini
tools.what: Google's general-purpose AI assistant, with a free tier and Workspace integration.
tools.why_for_layoff: Free. Drafts, summaries, and quick research; lives next to Gmail and Docs.

tools.name: Notion
tools.what: Workspace for notes, planning, and lightweight databases.
tools.why_for_layoff: Free for personal use. A good 'one place' for the job hunt — runway, target companies, story bank, follow-ups.

tools.name: Obsidian
tools.what: Local-first markdown notebook. Files live on your laptop, not in someone else's cloud.
tools.why_for_layoff: Free for personal use. No streaks, no nudges, no AI upsell. Quiet by design.

tools.name: GitHub
tools.what: Code hosting, version control, and a public portfolio surface.
tools.why_for_layoff: Free for unlimited public and private repos. Often the first thing a recruiter clicks.

tools.name: LeetCode
tools.what: Coding interview prep questions sorted by company and topic.
tools.why_for_layoff: Free tier covers most of what you need. Pace yourself — burnout solving Hards on a Sunday is real.

tools.name: HackerRank
tools.what: Coding challenges, certifications, and interview prep tracks.
tools.why_for_layoff: Free. Often the platform companies use for take-homes — practice in the real environment.

tools.name: Coursera
tools.what: Online courses and specializations from universities and companies.
tools.why_for_layoff: Most paid courses have a 'Financial Aid' application form — the form is right under the enroll button. They waive fees based on need.
tools.hardship_program: Apply via the 'Financial aid available' link on the course enrollment page; turnaround is usually under 15 days.

tools.name: edX
tools.what: Online courses from MIT, Harvard, and other universities; free audit option.
tools.why_for_layoff: Most courses can be audited for free — you lose the certificate but keep the lectures and materials.

tools.name: LinkedIn Learning
tools.what: Video courses on professional and technical skills.
tools.why_for_layoff: Free 1-month trial direct, OR free indefinitely via most US public library cards (search 'Gale Presents' on your library site).

tools.name: Insight Timer
tools.what: Meditation app with one of the largest free libraries online.
tools.why_for_layoff: Free without a paywall on the core library. No streaks. Use for the 4am spiral.

tools.name: 7 Cups
tools.what: Free emotional support from trained listeners over text chat, plus low-cost therapy.
tools.why_for_layoff: Free peer support is genuinely free. For the days when 'just call a friend' isn't going to happen.

tools.name: Lunchclub
tools.what: AI-matched 1:1 networking video calls based on what you're working on.
tools.why_for_layoff: Free. One curated intro per week is much less doom-y than trawling LinkedIn.

stacks.name: The silent-week stack
stacks.blurb: For when you haven't told anyone yet and don't want to optimize anything. Breathe first.

stacks.name: The free-stack
stacks.blurb: Everything 100% free forever. No credit card, no trial-then-bill.

stacks.name: Back to applying
stacks.blurb: The minimum stack to send five thoughtful applications a week without losing your mind.

stacks.name: The low-performance stack
stacks.blurb: No streaks, no progress nudges, no cheerful upsell. Quiet tools that won't make you perform recovery.
